- issues opened in `paper-repo`#5 ("Outline rev 9 vs the draft: three wording scopes in abstract/discussion") by `story-repo`  > I read abstract.tex, results.tex §3.4 and discussion.tex against Outline rev 9 (wiki). The results text already matches the outline (C6 no-evidence wording, absolute R², (e) 58%, 0.55). Three places claim more than the evidence:
  > 
  > 1. Abstract and discussion: "no score computed from the data predicts the bias better than a constant" / "no score computable from the data" — says no score exists. The result is for the scores tried (S̄, corner×estimated curvature, S_adj, degree benchmarks, Han–Ugander-style CV loss); results.tex says this correctly. Suggest: "none of the data-computable scores we tried predicts the bias better than a constant" (the intervals are wide; Brief rev. 8 P5 wording).
  > 2. Abstract: "Flexible learners do not beat the correctly specified regression" — scope it: on 12–14 cells per mechanism, fixed tunings, 200 draws per graph, with the threshold mechanism (d) as the exception (results.tex says so; abstract does not).
  > 3. Abstract: the Brief's headline pair is the regime map plus the bias non-identification. The abstract has both but states the bias as 'set by the response at the corners'; add 'which the data inside the observed exposure range do not identify (an interpretation consistent with every data-computable score failing, not a separate test)'. Also, if the abstract mentions degree-independence anywhere, it needs the mechanism qualifier (b falls, d rises then flat; holds for c, e, f); it does not now.
  > 
  > Not for the text yet: C9 (P6 sensitivity interval) and C6b (P7 confirmatory S_adj) are exploratory-after-results and are findings only if analysis reports them as run.
